The present First Appeal is filed by appellants - original claimants against the judgment and award dated 22.12.2006 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Sabarkantha at Himmatnagar in MACP NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4507/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:

sentences.text: Heard learned advocate Mr.Hiren Vyas for appellants and Ms. Kiran Pandey for respondent No.2.
Though served, none appeared for respondent No.3 3.

Brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1
On 23.03.1998, claimant No.1 and her deceased husband who was having his cycle with him coming towards Bharuch City.

While they were walking on the side of road towards Bharuch City, at around 6.00 p.m. one S.T. bus bearing registration No.GJ-1Z-3278 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed with deceased.
Resultantly, husband and claimant No.1 sustained serious injuries and succumbed due to injuries.
FIR was lodged against the driver of S.T. Bus at Bharuch Police Station.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4507/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined
3.2 Claimants filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/-.
Notices were served.
Opponent Nos.1 and 2 contested petition.
Pending application, opponent No.1-driver of S.T. bus was deleted vide Ex.20.
Opponent No.2 being Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation, appeared and filed Written Statement at Ex.19.
Issues were framed.
Claimant No.2 - father of deceased deposed himself vide Ex.25.

Claimants produced oral as well as documentary evidence such as salary slip,
Postmortem report, FIR.

After considering the oral as well documentary evidence, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition by directing opponents to pay Rs.4,73,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization with proportionate cost.

3.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award of compensation, appellants - original NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4507/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined claimants filed present First Appeal for enhancement of compensation.
4. Learned advocate for the appellants has submitted that the deceased was aged about 23 years at the time of accident and was possessing a technical qualification.
He was serving as a Work Assistant in a Private Company and drawing salary of Rs.3,445/- per month.
Salary slip has been produced at Ex.33.
However, learned Tribunal has not considered the salary slip and assessed notional income of deceased at Rs.2500/- per month.
Learned Tribunal has failed to award compensation under the head of future prospects.

Looking to the age of deceased, multiplier 12 which has been applied is on lower side and in view of settled law in the decision of Sarla Verma Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 12, multiplier 18 should have been applied.

5. Per contra, learned advocate for respondent has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4507/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined supported the award and submitted that in absence of any proof with regard to quantum of salary, learned Tribunal has properly assessed income of deceased at Rs.2,500/-.
The claimants, only by producing a salary slip at Ex.33, have not proved contents of document.
6. I have considered the submissions canvassed by learned advocates for parties and perused record and proceedings.
Deceased was aged about 23 years and was serving as a work assistant in a private company.
According to the salary slip at Ex.33, deceased was drawing salary of Rs.3,445/- per month.
As proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are summary in nature, strict proof as contemplated under the Evidence Act, is not required.
Considering the facts, it would be just and reasonable to consider income of deceased at Rs.3,445/- per month.

More particularly, there is absence of any challenge with regard to drawing of salary to the extent of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4507/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined Rs.3,445/-, I am of the view that it would be reasonable to assess income of Rs.3,445/- per month.

Considering the fact that the learned Tribunal has failed to award any compensation under the head of future prospects and the claimants are entitled to 50% future prospects addition as per settled law.
7. Considering the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma (supra) and age of deceased, multiplier adopted by learned Tribunal is not reasonable.
Hence, multiplier of 18 is applicable.

8. In view of the aforesaid discussions, the claimants are entitled to the following amount of compensation:-
Under the Head of Compensation of Rs.

Future loss of income Monthly income =
Rs.3,445/-
Future prospect 50% (Rs.3,445 + 50% = Rs.5,168/-) NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4507/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined Deduction 1/3rd (Rs.5168 - Rs.1723 = Rs.3445/) (Rs.3445 x 12 x 18) = Rs.7,44,120 7,44,120/-

Conventional Heads   Grand Total   Less awarded amount of   compensation by Tribunal  Enhanced amount   (Rs.8,14,120 - Rs.4,73,000/-)=
 Rs.3,41,120/-
 Interest   8.1
Claimants are entitled to enhanced amount of compensation of Rs.3,41,120/- @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till Gitaben.
